transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Rajiv (CTO), Emily (ML Eng), Carlos (Infra)
Shared: quantization deck (link), benchmark spreadsheet (placeholder link)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Samir, AE on the account, with lena our systems SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Rajiv: Hey thanks, all good. super excited, we basically hit throughput limits with FP16, want to see what quant can do without killing quality.
[00:12] Lena: cool, we'll focus today on tradeoffs across INT8, FP8, GPTQ and AWQ, plus specific notes about KV cache and batching since you said you do RAG.
[00:20] Emily: yes RAG heavy, lots of short-turn prompts and some long context for diagnostics. accuracy regressions are our main worry.
[00:28] Samir: understood. first slide, quick overview - INT8 gives biggest perf win on GPUs with good kernel support but may need per-channel scale for some layers; FP8 is emerging, better fidelity than naive INT8 but requires hw support and new runtime paths.
[00:42] Lena: (interrupt) also note GPTQ is a post-training quant that keeps most accuracy for many LLMs, but it's slower to produce and model-specific; AWQ gives a good middle-ground with less calibration work but slightly lower perf gains vs GPTQ in our tests.
[00:55] Carlos: real quick, how do these interact with KV cache? our app pins long-running sessions and reuses KV heavily.
[01:04] Lena: good question. KV cache is stored in FP16 usually; when we quantize weights we still keep KV in FP16 to avoid compounding error, otherwise you see latency regressions on long contexts. there's also cache eviction/batching interactions.
[01:22] Rajiv: ok so even if model is INT8 weights KV stays FP16? is that automatic?
[01:27] Lena: depends on the runtime; Redwood runtime by default keeps KV in FP16 unless you opt into fp8-kv mode — fp8-kv can reduce mem but we've seen more hallucinations over very long contexts.
[01:39] Emily: sounds like a tradeoff. performance numbers?
[01:42] Samir: we ran benchmarks on a 70B model: FP16 baseline p50 latency 180ms with batch1; INT8 reduced to ~120ms, throughput up ~1.6x. GPTQ (8-bit but layerwise calibrated) gave similar latency to INT8 but better token-level accuracy on LLaMA-family models. AWQ gave ~1.4x throughput with smaller quality loss vs naive INT8.
[01:58] Rajiv: was the eval on your internal prompts or standard benchmarks?
[02:01] Lena: internal + some public evals. we should run your eval set — you mentioned RAG with retrieval, that can highlight subtle regressions.
[02:08] Emily: can we quantify "subtle"? like exact metric drop.
[02:11] Lena: in our tests, GPTQ often keeps <1% relative drop on answer-exactness for many LLaMA2 derivatives, naive INT8 could be 2-5% on some instruction-heavy tasks. AWQ sits around 1.5-3% depending on calibration.
[02:25] Carlos: network wise, for on-prem with VPC, anything special for quantized models?
[02:29] Samir: not really model-specific, but binary artifact size changes — INT8/GPTQ artifacts are smaller which reduces transfer time to nodes. for private deployment we support image packages and model blobs stored in customer S3/VPC endpoints, plus KMS integration for keys.
[02:42] Rajiv: what about correctness drift after fine-tuning? we do continual fine-tune for domain tokens.
[02:47] Lena: if you fine-tune post-quant, you can see bigger regressions. best practice: fine-tune in FP16, then run GPTQ/AWQ on the finetuned checkpoint, re-evaluate on the eval set. avoid training on quantized weights.
[03:00] Emily: about GPTQ, how long does calibration take? and do you supply the tooling?
[03:04] Lena: calibration depends on model size and your sample set; for 70B it can take a few hours on a single high-memory GPU; Redwood includes scripts and we can run it as a service for pilot.
[03:13] Samir: note for production we recommend a small calibration set representative of RAG inputs — queries + long contexts — because KV and prefix tokens matter.
[03:21] Rajiv: latency SLOs: we need p99 < 400ms for interactive UI. with quant and batching how predictable is p99?
[03:28] Lena: batching increases throughput but can hurt p99 if you queue. Redwood supports latency-first routing: small batch windows for interactive routes and larger for background. with INT8 + small-batch policy we still meet p99 400ms on our Dedicated configs in our benchmarks.
[03:42] Emily: about batching and KV — any issues with dynamic prefixes? we have variable prefix lengths.
[03:46] Lena: runtime handles variable seq by padding and using continuous batching; however longer prefixes increase per-request compute because KV grows. again keeping KV in FP16 reduces error accumulation.
[03:55] Carlos: security — do quantized model blobs have any special compliance considerations?
[03:59] Samir: not really; it's still model weights. for Private we support encryption at rest via KMS/HSM, audit logs, and RBAC. we'll share SOC2 docs.
[04:09] Rajiv: you mentioned AWQ — can you explain the core difference vs GPTQ?
[04:13] Lena: AWQ (Adaptive Weight Quant) is more of a hybrid, it uses group-wise scaling with small FP blocks to preserve outliers; GPTQ is per-layer Hessian-aware rounding style calibration. AWQ tends to be faster to apply and is more robust on some MVL models but slightly less accurate than GPTQ on others.
[04:27] Emily: do you see model family differences? like Llama vs Mistral vs mixes?
[04:31] Lena: yes Mistral sometimes prefers FP8 or hybrid because of activation distributions; Llama-family tends to be very GPTQ-friendly. we have a model-compatibility matrix — we'll share.
[04:40] Samir: (shares screen) here's an example run: same prompt, FP16 answer high fidelity; INT8 slightly briefer; GPTQ keeps more detail.
[04:48] Rajiv: any mitigation for hallucinations introduced by quant?
[04:50] Lena: we recommend ensembles: run critical prompts on FP16 fallbacks or apply output scoring/regression checks with eval set; also temperature and sampling tweaks can compensate for verbosity changes. automatic fallback policies in Redwood can route to FP16 if a critical path shows quality drop.
[05:05] Emily: will fallback increase cost substantially?
[05:07] Samir: some, but often only a small fraction of traffic needs fallback if you pick conservative thresholds.
[05:12] Carlos: for on-prem pilot, what's the install timeline and footprint?
[05:16] Samir: install + model push can be done in a week for a single cluster node if networking and storage are ready; footprint depends on quant: INT8/GPTQ artifacts smaller by ~40-60% vs FP16 so infra RAM/disk is lower.
[05:28] Lena: one caution: if you use fp8 kv mode to shrink KV, it's experimental on certain GPUs; for Private we recommend sticking to FP16 KV until validated.
[05:36] Rajiv: let's talk metrics to validate: what should we run?
[05:39] Lena: we'll run accuracy (exact-match/F1 depending on tasks), latency p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec) with your traffic shape, and regression checks on your RAG hits. include long-run sessions to exercise KV.
[05:52] Emily: ok i'll extract 500 representative prompts and some long context threads.
[05:55] Samir: perfect. we'll run four configs: FP16 baseline, INT8 naive, GPTQ calibrated, AWQ hybrid. we'll return results with sample responses.
[06:05] Rajiv: any gotchas with SDKs/clients? we use a grpc client.
[06:09] Lena: Redwood supports REST + gRPC; for quantized models nothing changes client-side except if you want to request fallback or specific model variants via the route config.
[06:18] Emily: curious about cost savings ballpark?
[06:20] Samir: on Dedicated we see token-cost reductions ~30-60% depending on model and quant: INT8 high savings, GPTQ middle, AWQ middle-low. exact numbers tied to batching + KV choices. we'll include cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[06:33] Carlos: for network egress inside VPC, smaller model blobs help initial deployment but runtime traffic the same. micro-ops for half precision?
[06:40] Lena: runtime loads quantized kernels; no change in RPC size for token streams.
[06:44] Rajiv: last question: how do we track regressions over time when models update?
[06:48] Samir: Redwood Optimize can run eval suites on pin-targets and alert on regressions; for Private we can run eval agents and integrate with your CI to gate model rollouts.
[06:58] Emily: great, sounds like a plan.
[07:00] Samir: recap of next steps and action items — we'll send the spreadsheet and docs, you send eval set, lena schedules pilot kickoff. any other blockers?
[07:08] Rajiv: none immediate. thanks.
[07:10] Samir: thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts present; some proper nouns like "AWQ" and "GPTQ" were transcribed correctly but internal model names were simplified.
